## About
Targy's Tavern opened its doors shortly after the end of Prohibition, slightly off the beaten path in Upper Queen Anne. It was named for a longshoreman who worked Seattle's docks, Targelson, known to his friends as "Targy." The U-shaped bar top from those early days is still in place.
The building itself was put up with timber cut and milled from Queen Anne hill, and it first served as sleeping quarters for the crews running the horse-drawn counterbalance trolleys. Over the years the bar passed from Fran and Ed to Seattle bar legend Charlie Files, and in the spring a few years back Targy's joined the Stedman Group.
Today it's still a no-frills neighborhood bar on the corner of Crockett Street, open every day from late afternoon until close.

## Services
- Bingo with Kevin: Bingo night every Tuesday at 8 PM.
- Trivia with April: Trivia night every Wednesday evening.
- Happy hour: Happy hour runs Monday through Friday.
- Host a party: Thinking about hosting a party at Targy's? Get in touch and we'll work it out with you.

## FAQ
Q: Do you serve food, and can I bring my own?
A: We have a bar bites menu, and outside food is welcome too.

Q: Do you do anything for Seahawks games?
A: Yes, we run specials on Seahawks game days.
